en.name: Salted duck egg yolk
en.summary: These are the yolks of brine-cured duck eggs, sold loose or vacuum-packed, raw or already baked, for mooncakes, 蛋黃酥 and zongzi. Refrigerated they keep about 1 week; frozen, 3–4 months, which is the right way to keep a bag of them.
en.pantry: Separated yolks do not keep at room temperature. Salt-cured they may be, but a yolk lifted out of its shell and its brine has lost most of its protection and is a rich, low-acid food. Baked or steamed yolks should go straight from cooling into the fridge rather than sitting on a tray while you finish the pastry, and raw ones should never be left out at all. Follow the 2-hour rule, or 1 hour above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Keep the yolks in a sealed box at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and use them within about 1 week, whether they are raw, vacuum-packed or already baked. That figure is borrowed from what is published for hard-boiled eggs; no agency publishes one for salted yolks. Keep them separate from strong-smelling food — egg yolk picks up odours readily — and if they came in a vacuum pack, decant what you open into a covered box rather than trying to reseal it.
en.freezer: Freezing is the right way to keep a bag of yolks: 3–4 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze them in a single layer on a tray first, then bag them so they do not fuse into a lump. They come out slightly grainy, which does not matter once they are baked into a pastry or mashed into a sauce. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are a quality window, and it is the fat that eventually goes off-flavour.
en.thawing: Thaw the yolks in the fridge, not on the counter, and use them the same day. They can also go straight into a hot dish from frozen. Do not refreeze them.
spoilage: A rancid, paint-like or fishy smell — the fat has oxidised.
A grey, green or chalky-white surface instead of deep orange.
A slimy or sticky coating, or any mould.
A dry, crumbling yolk that has lost its oil, or a bitter taste.
tips: Freeze them on a tray first so they stay separate in the bag.
Label the bag with the date and whether they are raw or baked.
Keep them away from milk and butter in the fridge; the smell transfers.
Spritz raw yolks with a little rice wine before baking, as many bakers do, and use them that day.

faq.q: How long do salted egg yolks keep in the fridge?
faq.a: About 1 week at 4 °C or below, raw or baked. That is the hard-boiled egg figure applied here; no agency publishes one for salted yolks.

faq.q: Can you freeze salted egg yolks?
faq.a: Yes, 3–4 months at −18 °C, and it is the best way to keep them. Freeze them in a single layer first, then bag them.

faq.q: Do raw salted egg yolks need cooking?
faq.a: Yes. The salt cure is a seasoning, not a kill step, so bake or steam them before eating.

faq.q: Why have my salted egg yolks gone grainy?
faq.a: Freezing does that to the fat and protein. It makes no difference once they are baked into a pastry or mashed into a filling.

zh.name: 鹹蛋黃
zh.summary: 鹹蛋黃是鹽漬鴨蛋剝出來的蛋黃，散裝或真空包裝，有生的也有已經烤熟的，用來做月餅、蛋黃酥和粽子。冷藏大約可放 1 週；冷凍 3～4 個月，而後者才是保存一整包蛋黃的正確方式。
zh.pantry: 剝出來的蛋黃不耐室溫。它確實經過鹽漬，但一顆離開蛋殼和鹽水的蛋黃已經失去大部分保護，而且是油脂豐富、酸度又低的食物。烤過或蒸過的蛋黃放涼後就要直接進冰箱，不要一邊做酥皮一邊讓它在盤子上放著；生的更是完全不能放外面。請守 2 小時原則，超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。
zh.fridge: 密封盒裝放 4 °C 以下，約 1 週內用完，不管是生的、真空包的還是已經烤過的。這個數字借自水煮蛋的公告值；沒有機構公告過鹹蛋黃的期限。要和氣味重的食物分開放——蛋黃很會吸味；真空包拆開後請倒進有蓋容器，不要硬去重新封口。
zh.freezer: 一整包蛋黃的正確保存方式就是冷凍：−18 °C 下 3～4 個月。先單層排在盤上凍硬，再裝袋，才不會黏成一整團。解凍後質地略粗，但做成酥皮內餡或壓進醬汁完全不影響。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數是品質窗口，最終走味的是油脂。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍，不要放室溫，並當天用完。也可以直接從冷凍下熱鍋。不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 有油耗味、油漆味或腥味——油脂已經氧化。
表面泛灰、泛綠或變成粉白，而不是深橘色。
蛋黃乾硬碎裂、油脂盡失，或吃起來發苦。
tips: 先鋪盤單層凍硬再裝袋，才不會黏成一塊。
袋上標日期，並註明是生的還是烤過的。
冰箱裡遠離牛奶和奶油；氣味會轉移。
生蛋黃入烤箱前噴一點米酒（很多烘焙師傅的做法），並當天用完。

faq.q: 鹹蛋黃冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 不論生熟，放 4 °C 以下約 1 週。這是水煮蛋的數字套用過來；鹹蛋黃本身沒有公告值。
可以，−18 °C 下 3～4 個月，而且這是最好的保存方式。先單層凍硬再裝袋。
需要。鹽漬是調味不是殺菌步驟，請先烤過或蒸過再吃。

faq.q: 鹹蛋黃為什麼變得粗粗沙沙的？
faq.a: 冷凍會讓油脂和蛋白質產生這種變化。烤成酥皮內餡或壓成餡料之後完全吃不出來。
